cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: WiFi signal ≠ cable – a facility allowing computers or smartphones to connect to the internet wirelessly.

p.em: Example: Standard WiFi signals can bounce off human bodies to identify individuals.

cosy-blockquote.p: Accuracy ≠ error – the quality or state of being correct or precise.

p.em: Example: The new system identifies people with near-perfect accuracy.

cosy-blockquote.p: Detection ≠ ignorance – the action or process of identifying the presence of something.

p.em: Example: WiFi-based detection works through solid walls without cameras.

cosy-blockquote.p: Biometric ≠ password – relating to the measurement and analysis of unique physical characteristics.

p.em: Example: Gait and body shape serve as invisible biometric markers.

cosy-blockquote.p: Surveillance ≠ privacy – close observation, especially by a government or organization.

p.em: Example: WiFi tracking raises fresh concerns about invisible surveillance.

cosy-blockquote.p: Distortion ≠ clarity – the action of giving a misleading account or impression.

p.em: Example: Body movements create distinct distortion patterns in radio waves.

cosy-blockquote.p: Receiver ≠ transmitter – an apparatus for receiving incoming radio signals.

p.em: Example: The router receiver analyzes signal fluctuations instantly.

cosy-blockquote.p: Intrusion ≠ security – an unwelcome infiltration into a personal environment.

p.em: Example: Unseen tracking is seen by many as a privacy intrusion.

cosy-blockquote.p: Authentication ≠ denial – the process or action of proving something to be genuine.

p.em: Example: WiFi biometrics could replace password authentication for smart homes.

cosy-blockquote.p: Passive ≠ active – accepting or allowing what happens without active response.

p.em: Example: Passive tracking requires no wearable devices or user action.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
How can a ambient WiFi signal be used to reconstruct indoor human body posture?
★ Does the idea of spatial wave reflection tracking amaze or worry you?

What level of mathematical accuracy is required for motion-sensing algorithms?
★ How reliable are your smart home motion sensors?

How does early detection of unusual movement patterns assist elderly care?
★ Would you use non-camera motion sensors to keep elderly relatives safe?

Why is gait analysis considered a unique biometric identifier like fingerprints?
★ How distinctive do you think your walking style is?

What are the ethical implications of commercial surveillance using existing internet infrastructure?
★ Are you concerned about passive data collection in public spaces?

How does physical wall distortion affect high-frequency radio wave reception?
★ Have you noticed signal drops near dense building materials?

What is the role of a wireless signal receiver in processing reflected waves?
★ Are you interested in signal processing physics?

How can smart homes prevent unauthorized digital intrusion through smart sensors?
★ What security measures do you use on your home network?

Why is two-factor authentication crucial for network privacy?
★ Do you use 2FA on all your primary accounts?

What is the advantage of passive sensing over active video camera monitoring?
★ Do you prefer radar-based motion detection over visible video cameras?

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, work together on the following task:

cosy-blockquote.p: A comparative reflection on our habits and self-perceptions.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: 1-on-1 guided visual description and task response with teacher.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Look at the prompt and discuss your response with your teacher:

cosy-blockquote.p: A comparative reflection on our habits and self-perceptions.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
Using ambient WiFi signal disturbance for spatial monitoring is superior to optical camera surveillance. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you choose wave-based monitoring over video cameras?

High algorithmic accuracy in movement tracking justifies minor privacy trade-offs. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Willing to trade privacy for enhanced security?

Automated falls detection in smart homes will transform eldercare globally. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you install motion sensors for aging parents?

Gait-based biometric recognition will soon replace traditional physical keys and passwords. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Look forward to keyless biometric entry doors?

Mass commercial surveillance via public Wi-Fi access points must be outlawed. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Support strict laws against spatial tracking?

Preventing wave distortion through solid walls is the main obstacle for indoor radar tech. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Interested in architectural technology?

Installing a sensitive signal receiver in every room will become standard in modern architecture. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Want smart motion-sensing light switches in every room?

Undetectable spatial intrusion poses a greater threat to personal privacy than camera leaks. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Which feels more invasive : cameras or wave tracking?

Multi-factor authentication should be legally mandated for all internet of things devices. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Should hardware makers enforce strong default passwords?

Deploying passive environmental monitoring will make smart homes significantly safer. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Are smart security systems worth their cost?

Incorrect: It identify people with accuracy. → Correct: It identifies people with high accuracy / accurately. ((3rd person singular present simple verb requires '-s': 'identifies'.))
